passage: Mentor's note, Sunday. Amandeep has cut each weeknight into three blocks of an hour and a half, with short breaks between them, and pinned a wall chart above the desk: a tick for each block done, a dot for each one missed. I watched the chart fill through Thursday. Two dots sat next to organic chemistry. In earlier weeks the missed items simply vanished from the list. Today Amandeep sat down with a pencil and moved both topics to next week's first block instead of pretending they were done. I asked how many dots would be acceptable; Amandeep said two a week, no more. I will look at the chart again next Sunday and ask about the chemistry. — Vandana

passage:
Sunday, 9 pm

Week three of the new system, and I finally trust it.

Every evening now has three blocks of ninety minutes: 5 to 6:30, 7 to 8:30, 9 to 10:30. Each block gets one topic, written the night before. There's a chart on my wall with a box for each block. Green tick if done, red cross if not. No half-ticks. Bidisha said that's harsh, but it's honest.

This week: fifteen blocks, twelve green, three red. Organic chemistry twice (I underestimated it), and one physics block I lost to a power cut.

The old me would've just skipped those topics and hoped. Tonight I did the Sunday review instead. I moved all three red topics into next week's plan, first thing Monday and Tuesday, before anything new.

I'm Minakshi, and I feel calmer than I have all year. Nothing is quietly disappearing anymore.

qa.q: How many blocks were green this week?
How does Minakshi feel about the new system?
qa.a: Minakshi feels calmer than all year, trusting the system now.

qa.q: What else could Minakshi do about the organic chemistry blocks?
qa.a: Minakshi could plan longer or extra blocks for organic chemistry, since it was underestimated twice.

qa.q: How might Bidisha see the chart's no-half-ticks rule?
qa.a: Bidisha finds it harsh, but may come to see it is honest and helps nothing get quietly skipped.

grounding: A diary shows a student dividing evenings into three ninety-minute blocks, marking each on a wall chart and moving unfinished topics into next week at a Sunday review.
